He calls the Spirit's gift the ability to speak in tongues, that is, to have the power of speaking in languages; if I pray in the Spirit, that is, having used the language given through the Spirit, my mind will be unfruitful; for in prayers, one must strive together and seek the things that lead to salvation from God, not to be puffed up by language and simply to speak in tongues; since the mind becomes unfruitful, not receiving any benefit from such ambition; I will pray in the Spirit, I will pray also with the mind; it is necessary for me, if I wish to pray in tongues, that is, to be approved in speaking in tongues, to strive earnestly not to have an unfruitful mind, nor to be alone in speaking in tongues, but to arouse my mind; and if I were to sing in tongues, I would not neglect to understand the power of the psalm and the prophecy with my mind; for if I were to speak empty sounds, I would be like a sounding brass; therefore, it is better to prophesy or interpret the divine scriptures in the church than to simply speak in tongues; what then is the better thing? I will pray in the Spirit, I will pray also with the mind; and again, the Spirit here refers to the gift of the Spirit; since his goal is to show that speaking in tongues is not beneficial unless it is accompanied by the ability to interpret the prophets, he adds other things by which one can clearly see what is being said

For if you bless with the spirit, the one filling the place of the layperson, how will he say 'Amen'? When you speak in a tongue, the one filled in the order of the laity, if he does not know your voice, how will he assent to the 'Amen' in his own prayers? For it is clear in all churches that the prayers of the leaders are followed by the assent of those under their care. They assent to the 'Amen' with their own petitions to God, bringing to completion the voice of the priest, so that what seems to be lacking in the perfection of the priests is filled by the measures of the people, and God receives the small with the great in unity of spirit. For the people under their care, joining their own prayers to those of the priests, have believed they will be accepted. To this end, God has also commanded that poor sacrifices be brought to the altar, so that the small, mixed with the perfect, may become acceptable to God. For we are all one in the Lord. When, therefore, you speak in a tongue, this is to bless with the spirit. The one who does not know what you are saying, how will he say 'Amen' to his own prayer? You may act correctly, according to your own mind, but the other person is not edified. But all things must be done for our edification and for the benefit of our brothers.

pass_b_english: The gift of the Spirit is the ability to speak in tongues, which is the power to speak in languages.
If I pray in the Spirit, using the language given through the Spirit, my mind will be unfruitful.
In prayers, one must strive together and seek the things that lead to salvation from God, not to be puffed up by language and simply to speak in tongues.
For if I were to speak empty sounds, I would be like a sounding brass (1 Corinthians 13:1).
For if I were to speak in tongues without understanding, my mind would be unfruitful, and I would not receive any benefit from such ambition.
I will pray in the Spirit, and I will also pray with my mind.
If I wish to pray in tongues, I must strive earnestly not to have an unfruitful mind, nor to be alone in speaking in tongues, but to arouse my mind.
And if I were to sing in tongues, I would not neglect to understand the power of the psalm and the prophecy with my mind.
For it is better to prophesy or interpret the divine scriptures in the church than to simply speak in tongues.
What then is the better thing? I will pray in the Spirit, and I will pray also with my mind.
When we bless with the spirit, the person who is taking the place of the layperson cannot say 'Amen' because they do not understand what is being said.
This is a problem because, in the churches, it is customary for the people to follow the prayers of their leaders with their own assent, bringing to completion the voice of the priest.
By doing so, what seems to be lacking in the perfection of the priests is filled by the measures of the people, and God receives both the small and the great in unity of spirit.
The people under their care join their own prayers to those of the priests, believing that they will be accepted by God.
This is why God has also commanded that even poor sacrifices be brought to the altar, so that the small, mixed with the perfect, may become acceptable to God.
For we are all one in the Lord.
And when we speak in a tongue, we are blessing with the spirit.
However, if the person listening does not know what we are saying, they cannot say 'Amen' to their own prayer, and therefore they are not edified.
It is essential that all things be done for our edification and for the benefit of our brothers.
The proclamation of all good things is truly for those who have received faith.
In this proclamation, it is said that they stand firm and are saved.
The fact that they stand indicates that they have stability in their hope and are in a state of good glory, having believed.
And the fact that they are saved means that this salvation has also been revealed to them.
